messages.author: 9e5837f0d144e8f1
messages.subject: question about data output
parts:
Hi,
After I output a data frame to a txt file using "write.table" command, I found that it always shows an "x" in the first row, which my data frame does not contain.
Why there is an "x"? How to eliminate the "x"?
Thanks!

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] question about data output
parts:
Hm, with this, I don't have that problem:

x <- data.frame(QWE=1:5, ASD=letters[1:5])
write.table(x, file="x.txt", quote=FALSE, sep="\t")

The output file looks fine.

STG

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] question about data output
parts:
Oh, a table, yes, that happens as the default as described in the
book. write.table converts a table into a data frame first and that
makes the first column be called Var1, for instance:

qwe <- table(sample(letters[1:5], 100, replace=TRUE))
write.table(qwe, file="x.txt", row.names=FALSE, col.names=TRUE, quote=FALSE)

Thus, if you make it a data frame yourself, you can tweak the names:

asd <-as.data.frame(qwe); names(asd)[1] <- "whateveryouwant"
write.table(asd, file="x.txt", row.names=FALSE, col.names=TRUE, quote=FALSE)

STG
